content:
Fireflies.ai transcription

Meeting: Arkadia Finance — Optimize Suggestions beta check-in
Date/Time: Feb 20, 2026 4:00 PM ET
Duration: 43 minutes

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Miguel Santos (Customer Success), Aditya Rao (PM, Optimize), Kenji Nakamura (Product Design)
Arkadia Finance: Priya Desai (Platform Eng Mgr), Evan Cho (Staff ML Eng), Marta Klein (FinOps), Samir Qureshi (SRE)

---
Summary (auto-generated)
- Arkadia is generally excited about the Suggestions view, but several parts were confusing: what “Risk” means, why some high-savings items are labeled Medium/High, and how to reconcile estimated savings with billing.
- Arkadia requested additional filtering (project, route, model version, region, and time window) and a way to export/share results internally.
- Redwood clarified the current beta scope (batching/caching only), that savings are estimates not guarantees, and that risk refers to performance/reliability impact.
- Next steps agreed: Redwood to provide documentation + validate estimator assumptions for Arkadia’s account; Arkadia to provide SLO context and run a canary change on a single route.

Topics
1) What Arkadia likes / what’s working
2) Confusions: risk level, savings accuracy, and “why this recommendation” content
3) Requested filters + sharing workflow
4) Safe rollout: canary, guardrails, and who should have access
5) Next steps and timeline

Action items
- Miguel Santos: Send docs + “Risk levels explained” one-pager and the recommended validation workflow for beta suggestions (by 2026-02-21).
- Aditya Rao: Investigate Arkadia’s “estimate doesn’t match billing” example and reply with findings + any mitigations (by 2026-02-25).
- Kenji Nakamura: Capture and prioritize UI filter/export requests; propose table filter set for next iteration (by 2026-02-24).
- Samir Qureshi: Share top routes, latency SLOs, and any routes that are “no touch” due to incident sensitivity (by 2026-02-23).

Questions (captured)
- Does “Risk” include security/compliance risk? (No; it’s performance/reliability/quality risk.)
- Can we filter by environment (prod vs staging) and project? (Not in the current beta UI; Redwood will log and plan.)
- Can we validate savings on a small sample without committing to a global config change? (Yes; use canary/rollout controls on a single route.)
- Why do some suggestions say “insufficient telemetry” when we have high traffic? (Usually ingestion lag or missing required signals; Redwood to confirm for Arkadia.)

---
Transcript

[00:00] Miguel Santos: Alright, cool. I think we’re recording. Thanks everyone for making time. This is our Arkadia Suggestions beta check-in. The goal today is just hear what’s working, what’s confusing, and line up next steps.

[00:14] Priya Desai: Sounds good.

[00:15] Miguel Santos: Quick intros on our side—Miguel, customer success. Aditya is PM for Optimize. Kenji is design.

[00:23] Aditya Rao: Hey everyone.

[00:24] Kenji Nakamura: Hi.

[00:25] Priya Desai: Priya, I run platform engineering here. Evan from ML engineering, Marta from FinOps, Samir from SRE.

[00:33] Evan Cho: Hey.

[00:34] Marta Klein: Hi.

[00:35] Samir Qureshi: Hello.

[00:37] Miguel Santos: Great. Maybe we start with—what did you actually do in the beta so far? Like which routes did you look at.

[00:45] Evan Cho: We looked at two main things. One was our chat completion endpoint for internal analysts. The other is embeddings for doc retrieval. The Suggestions page popped up like “batching opportunity” and then also “prefix caching” I think.

[01:00] Kenji Nakamura: Mm-hmm.

[01:01] Evan Cho: The UI is pretty clean. The list is helpful. But the risk label was… we got stuck on that. Like it says “Medium risk” and my leadership immediately asked, is that security risk? Is that like compliance risk? And I’m like, I don’t think so, but it’s not obvious.

[01:18] Miguel Santos: Yep, that’s a really common question. In this beta, risk is strictly performance and reliability risk. Not security. Not data exposure. It’s basically: “if you apply this, how likely are you to move your p95 latency or timeouts in a bad direction” and how confident we are about that.

[01:34] Samir Qureshi: The word “risk” in our org is loaded. We have risk committees. So when I dropped the screenshot in Slack, people were like, who approved this, you know.

[01:43] Kenji Nakamura: That’s really good feedback. We’ve debated alternate labels too, like “impact” or “latency risk.” We can also add a tooltip that explicitly says “performance/reliability risk.”

[01:56] Priya Desai: Tooltip would help. Also the “why” text in the drawer—some of it reads like marketing. Sorry. Like “you can save up to X.” And then later it says estimates aren’t guaranteed. Our FinOps team wants the math.

[02:11] Marta Klein: Yeah. I’m the annoying one. We need to explain the assumptions. Like, what time window? Are you using our contracted rate? Are you using list price? What about retries? We have a lot of retries in one region.

[02:24] Aditya Rao: Not annoying at all. That’s exactly what we want to get right before GA. In the current beta, the estimator uses your observed tokens and request volume from the telemetry window—typically last 7 days, but it can be shorter if you don’t have a full week of clean signals. Then we apply a token price assumption based on your Redwood billing plan, not list price. But there are edge cases if the route mixes models or if some traffic isn’t attributed cleanly.

[02:49] Marta Klein: Okay. Because we saw one suggestion that said roughly “$1,200/day savings” and I’m like… that’s basically our entire daily spend on that service. So it didn’t pass the sniff test.

[03:00] Miguel Santos: Got it. That’s important.

[03:02] Aditya Rao: Do you remember which suggestion it was? Like batching vs caching.

[03:05] Evan Cho: It was batching. It said something like “enable continuous batching for route /chat/analyst” and then showed a big number.

[03:14] Samir Qureshi: And it was also marked “High risk,” which made it harder to socialize. People were like, why are we taking a high risk thing to save money.

[03:23] Kenji Nakamura: So there are two things there: the savings magnitude and the risk label. The risk label is trying to warn that the route is low-latency sensitive and you have spiky concurrency. But if the savings number is off, then the whole thing loses credibility.

[03:39] Priya Desai: Exactly.

[03:41] Miguel Santos: Before we go too deep, can I ask: how did you want to use this internally? Like who is the end user. You? FinOps? SRE?

[03:50] Priya Desai: It’s shared. Platform owns config. ML owns the prompts and models. FinOps is pushing cost reduction targets. SRE wants guardrails.

[03:59] Samir Qureshi: And I’m not going to approve anything that could move p95 by 200ms without a canary.

[04:04] Miguel Santos: Totally. And the beta explicitly doesn’t auto-apply anything. It should always be a “you choose to apply” and ideally via your rollout controls.

[04:13] Aditya Rao: For batching, the risk is often about tail latency and queueing. So the safe workflow is: pick one route, apply a conservative cap—like max batch size, max queue delay—and then canary 5% traffic. Watch p95 and error rate.

[04:30] Samir Qureshi: That’s what I want to see reflected in the UI. Like “recommended guardrails” as part of the suggestion.

[04:36] Kenji Nakamura: We can add a section in the drawer: “Suggested rollout plan” or “Recommended guardrails.”

[04:42] Evan Cho: Also filters. The list is hard because it’s like everything across regions and projects. We need to slice it. Like, I only care about prod, us-east, this one project.

[04:55] Priya Desai: Yeah. At minimum filter by project, route, and region. And model version would be huge because we have two versions pinned.

[05:04] Kenji Nakamura: Noted. Right now we have basic filters, but not all of those. The table design can accommodate chips—Project, Route, Model, Region, and maybe “Suggestion type.”

[05:16] Marta Klein: And a time filter. Like “last 24 hours” vs “last 7 days.” Because our traffic is not stable. Month-end is crazy.

[05:26] Aditya Rao: We don’t have a time window selector in the UI today. Under the hood we compute on a fixed cadence and we show a “stale as of” timestamp, but it’s kind of subtle.

[05:35] Evan Cho: I saw “as of” but I didn’t know what it meant. I assumed it was when the UI loaded.

[05:40] Kenji Nakamura: That’s on us. Copy issue.

[05:43] Miguel Santos: Okay, so: filters and clearer staleness messaging.

[05:47] Samir Qureshi: Another confusion: the risk label. You say it’s performance risk, but it’s not clear how it’s calculated. We got a “Medium risk” caching suggestion which felt safer than batching, but it didn’t explain why medium.

[06:02] Aditya Rao: For caching, “risk” is usually around correctness and cache churn. Like if your prompts have a lot of dynamic prefixes, or you have low repeat rate, you might not get hits and you might add overhead. Also if you’re close to memory limits, enabling caching may increase pressure and cause evictions.

[06:20] Evan Cho: Right, and we’d like to see the inputs. Like “repeat rate is X, estimated hit rate uplift Y.”

[06:29] Aditya Rao: Makes sense. We can show the top few signals: observed prefix reuse, concurrency distribution, latency sensitivity classification.

[06:38] Kenji Nakamura: That’s consistent with “show assumptions and confidence.” We can add an “Inputs” accordion.

[06:43] Marta Klein: Please. Because otherwise it reads like a black box.

[06:47] Miguel Santos: On the savings mismatch—Marta, do you have a specific example we can look at offline? Like screenshot plus which date range.

[06:55] Marta Klein: I can send a screenshot. The suggestion drawer had that $1,200/day number. Our billing report for that route was like $800/day total. So “savings” can’t exceed spend. Unless you’re including other routes.

[07:10] Aditya Rao: Yeah, savings should never exceed baseline spend for that scope. That sounds like a scoping bug—maybe route aggregation includes more traffic than the UI label indicates. Or a currency/units issue.

[07:24] Miguel Santos: We’ve seen one other instance of “scope mismatch” where a route name is aliased, like /chat/analyst and /chat/analyst/stream.

[07:33] Evan Cho: We do have both.

[07:34] Aditya Rao: That could explain it. If the baseline is combining both but the label is one. I’ll dig in.

[07:40] Priya Desai: Thank you.

[07:42] Miguel Santos: Anything else on confusion?

[07:44] Samir Qureshi: Access control. I could see suggestions, but one of our ML engineers couldn’t. Not sure if it’s role based.

[07:52] Miguel Santos: It is RBAC-scoped. We can check what permission is required. Usually it’s “Optimize: read suggestions.” We can get that fixed.

[08:02] Priya Desai: That’s fine, just tell us what roles should have it.

[08:06] Kenji Nakamura: From UX perspective we also want a nicer “permission denied” page, not just a generic error.

[08:12] Evan Cho: The error was like, “forbidden.” Not super helpful.

[08:15] Miguel Santos: Got it.

[08:17] Priya Desai: Big picture though: we want this. We’ve looked at Bedrock and Azure OpenAI cost dashboards. They show spend but not “what to do.” This is the “what to do.” It just has to be defensible.

[08:33] Miguel Santos: That’s encouraging.

[08:34] Aditya Rao: That’s exactly the intention.

[08:37] Miguel Santos: Let’s talk about requested features. Filters: project, route, region, model version, environment, time window.

[08:47] Kenji Nakamura: Environment is tricky depending on how it’s tagged, but project/route/region/model are straightforward.

[08:54] Evan Cho: Also “sort by savings” is good but we want “sort by risk” and “sort by confidence.”

[08:59] Kenji Nakamura: We have sort for savings right now; risk sort is on our list.

[09:05] Marta Klein: And export. I need to take it to a meeting. Screenshot is not enough; we need a CSV, even if it’s just top 20.

[09:13] Miguel Santos: That’s helpful. A lot of customers ask for export.

[09:17] Samir Qureshi: One more: show the rollout guardrails. If it says “enable batching,” it should also say “max queue delay 2ms” or whatever you think is safe.

[09:29] Aditya Rao: We can propose defaults, but we have to be careful. Because safe values vary based on route SLO.

[09:36] Samir Qureshi: Right. But even “start with conservative: queue delay <= 5ms, max batch size <= 8” is better than nothing.

[09:46] Aditya Rao: Agreed. We can phrase as “starting point” and encourage canary.

[09:52] Kenji Nakamura: We can also add a link to the exact config page with those fields highlighted.

[09:58] Evan Cho: Deep link would be great. Today I had to go find the batching config.

[10:03] Miguel Santos: Cool. So far: better risk label, show signals/assumptions, filters, export, and rollout guardrails.

[10:12] Miguel Santos: Can we also ask about the copy. Would “Performance risk” be enough? Or “Latency/reliability risk.”

[10:18] Priya Desai: “Latency/reliability risk” is clearer. Because “performance risk” could still be interpreted weirdly.

[10:25] Samir Qureshi: Yeah, say “latency + errors” basically.

[10:29] Kenji Nakamura: Noted.

[10:31] Marta Klein: And please put “estimated” next to savings everywhere. Not just once.

[10:38] Miguel Santos: Yep. We’re aligned there.

[10:41] Evan Cho: One thing I liked: it had “confidence” but I didn’t know what to do with it. Like is it statistical confidence.

[10:49] Aditya Rao: It’s not a p-value. It’s basically how complete the telemetry is and how stable the workload is. So if your distribution is changing a lot, or you don’t have enough samples, we reduce confidence.

[11:05] Evan Cho: Makes sense. If you can show “needs more telemetry” or “high variance in QPS” that would help.

[11:12] Aditya Rao: Yes.

[11:14] Miguel Santos: Switching gears: do you want to run an experiment off one suggestion? Like pick a route and we can do the safe rollout.

[11:21] Priya Desai: We can do caching on embeddings first. That seems less scary.

[11:26] Samir Qureshi: Agree. Batching on chat is the scary one.

[11:29] Marta Klein: If caching gives even 10% savings that’s meaningful.

[11:34] Aditya Rao: Great. For embeddings, do you have a lot of repeated prefixes? Actually embeddings are usually shorter, so caching depends on how you call it.

[11:43] Evan Cho: We have a lot of repeated system text and metadata. But user text changes.

[11:49] Aditya Rao: Ok, so we might see partial reuse. We’ll look at your telemetry. If the suggestion exists, it probably detected some repeat rate.

[12:01] Miguel Santos: Samir, if you do a canary, what’s your typical approach?

[12:05] Samir Qureshi: We do 5% for an hour, then 25% for a day, then 100%. We monitor p50/p95 latency, 5xx, and timeouts. We also watch GPU utilization because memory issues show up as weird latency spikes.

[12:19] Miguel Santos: Perfect. That aligns with what we recommend.

[12:23] Kenji Nakamura: If you send us your SLO numbers, we can tailor what the UI should say, like “your p95 target is 800ms.”

[12:31] Priya Desai: We can share the top 3 routes and their targets.

[12:36] Miguel Santos: Great.

[12:38] Marta Klein: Another request: show baseline spend in the drawer. Then “estimated savings” is contextual. Right now it’s just savings.

[12:47] Kenji Nakamura: That’s a good point. Like “current cost: $X/day; estimated after: $Y/day.”

[12:54] Aditya Rao: That also acts as a sanity check, to avoid savings > baseline.

[12:59] Miguel Santos: Exactly.

[13:01] Evan Cho: Also model names. The suggestion sometimes just says “llama-something” but we have a pinned version. We need exact version.

[13:09] Aditya Rao: Understood. We can show model + version in the table and drawer.

[13:14] Priya Desai: Do you support multiple deployments? We have dedicated in one region and hosted fallback.

[13:20] Miguel Santos: Yep. Suggestions should be scoped to your org/project and the routes. It can include region and capacity tier. In beta we’re still making sure the routing dimension is represented cleanly.

[13:34] Samir Qureshi: That’s another point. If it recommends caching, does it assume the same in dedicated and hosted? Because performance differs.

[13:42] Aditya Rao: Good catch. The estimate is calculated per route and per environment dimension we have. If it’s blending, that’s a bug.

[13:51] Miguel Santos: We’ll verify for your account specifically.

[13:55] Marta Klein: Sorry, one more. We’ve been burned by vendors promising savings. I want an explicit sentence: “not a commitment.”

[14:04] Miguel Santos: We can do that. We’ll share docs that are very explicit: estimates only.

[14:10] Kenji Nakamura: And we can make sure that sentence is in-product, not only docs.

[14:15] Priya Desai: Great.

[14:17] Miguel Santos: Okay. We’re at about halfway. Let me recap what I heard and you tell me if I missed anything.

[14:24] Miguel Santos: 1) Risk label is confusing—people interpret as security/compliance risk. Need clearer label and tooltip, “latency/reliability risk.” 2) Savings numbers must be defensible: show baseline cost, show assumptions, show scope; also fix potential scope bug. 3) Add filters: project, route, region, model version, environment, and time window. 4) Add export/share. 5) Add rollout guardrails + deep link to config.

[14:52] Priya Desai: That’s accurate.

[14:54] Evan Cho: Yep.

[14:55] Marta Klein: Yes.

[14:56] Samir Qureshi: Yeah.

[14:58] Aditya Rao: Great. On the estimator mismatch, I’ll take that as my action. If you can send the screenshot and the route names, we’ll pull logs and confirm.

[15:07] Marta Klein: I’ll send after this.

[15:09] Miguel Santos: Thank you.

[15:11] Miguel Santos: Any other feature requests? Even if out of scope.

[15:14] Evan Cho: Quantization. I know you said beta is caching/batching only. But leadership asked “where is quantization.”

[15:21] Aditya Rao: Yep. Not in this beta view. We’re working on it, but we don’t want to overload the UI until we trust the estimator and guardrails.

[15:29] Priya Desai: That’s fine, just don’t hide it. Maybe a “coming soon” section.

[15:34] Kenji Nakamura: We can do a placeholder, but we need to be careful about expectations.

[15:39] Miguel Santos: We can frame as “future: quantization suggestions” without implying availability.

[15:44] Samir Qureshi: Also, show “last computed” prominently. If this job is daily, we need to know.

[15:51] Aditya Rao: It’s typically hourly to daily depending on data availability. In your case it should be daily right now.

[15:58] Evan Cho: Then show that.

[16:00] Kenji Nakamura: Noted.

[16:02] Miguel Santos: Alright. Next steps: we’ll send docs, investigate the savings number, and we’ll circle back in two weeks. Does that work?

[16:10] Priya Desai: Works.

[16:11] Samir Qureshi: Works.

[16:12] Marta Klein: Works.

[16:14] Miguel Santos: Great. Anything you want from us besides the docs and the investigation?

[16:18] Priya Desai: If you can give us a short blurb we can paste internally: what this is, what it isn’t. Like two paragraphs.

[16:27] Miguel Santos: Yes. I’ll include that.

[16:30] Kenji Nakamura: And if you’re open, we’d love to do a quick usability follow-up. Like 20 minutes, watch you use filters—well, once we have them.

[16:38] Priya Desai: Sure.

[16:40] Evan Cho: Yeah.

[16:42] Miguel Santos: Perfect. We’ll set that up after the next iteration.

[16:47] Miguel Santos: Okay, I’ll stop recording. Thanks everyone.

---
Notes
- Customer emphasized internal stakeholder sensitivity to the term “risk.” They want explicit “latency/reliability risk” wording.
- Customer strongly requested baseline spend display and more transparent estimator assumptions.
- Customer intends to test caching first via canary; batching on chat is considered higher operational risk.
